issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT silently duplicated as private constant — invariant that the on-disk format uses the SAME shift as Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat is no longer enforced by the type system
issues.detail: The original code referenced Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat.DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT via static import. The move introduces a new constant Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16 in the backward_codecs package, and the writer now imports it from there. There is no compile-time or runtime check that these two constants remain equal. If the core constant is ever changed (a reasonable evolution in a non-frozen format), the legacy reader will silently mis-decode existing indexes because the precondition 'shift used at read time equals shift used at write time' is no longer expressible. The author cannot state an invariant tying these two values together; the duplication is exactly the kind of unstated precondition Dijkstra refuses.
issues.lines: around the new 'static final int DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16;' declaration

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException — a smuggled goto out of a method whose declared contract is to return a writer
issues.detail: Both Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.fieldsWriter and Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.fieldsWriter now unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. The method's postcondition ('returns a non-null FlatVectorsWriter for state') is unsatisfiable, yet the type signature still advertises it. This is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE: the precondition 'this format may be used for writing' is not represented in the type system, and the runtime exception is the only line of defense. The correct discipline is to expose a read-only interface (split the format), or at minimum assert at construction time that the SPI is not selected as a writeable format in the active codec. The current design relies on testing each write path to discover the misuse.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation removed from both legacy formats — the deprecation signal to downstream users is lost just as the format is being frozen
issues.detail: The previous code marked both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat as @Deprecated. The diff strips this annotation. Moving a class to backward_codecs is precisely when @Deprecated becomes most informative for users still referencing the old fully-qualified name during migration. Removing it weakens the compile-time warning that should accompany this lifecycle transition. State the postcondition plainly: 'users must not write with this format'; the language has an annotation for that.

issues.description: numMergeWorkers and mergeExec constructor parameters are now accepted and silently discarded
issues.detail: The HNSW format constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec, validates them (throwing on inconsistent combinations), and then... does nothing with them, because the fields were removed along with the writer. The validation logic survives but its postcondition ('the passed executor will be used for merges') no longer holds. Parameters that are validated but ignored are a classic source of caller confusion: the contract advertised by the signature contradicts the behavior. Either remove the parameters from the constructor (since writing is unsupported anyway) or remove the validation. Keeping both is incoherent.
issues.lines: constructor around the removed numMergeWorkers/mergeExec assignments

issues.description: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues field visibility silently downgraded from protected to package-private while the class remains public and non-final
issues.detail: The fields dimension, size, numBytes, scalarQuantizer, similarityFunction, vectorsScorer, compress, slice, binaryValue, byteBuffer, byteSize, lastOrd, scoreCorrectionConstant were 'protected' and are now package-private (no modifier). The class is still 'public abstract', so subclasses outside the package can be written by callers — but they can no longer access these fields. This is a breaking change to the inheritance contract that is not justified anywhere in the diff. Either make the class package-private/sealed (so the new visibility is provable as safe), or restore protected. As written, the precondition for subclassing has been quietly tightened.
issues.lines: field declarations near top of class

issues.description: SPI registers a non-writeable format that will throw on any write attempt — fail-fast moved from load time to write time
issues.detail: The module-info and META-INF/services register Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat as KnnVectorsFormat providers. A user can construct an IndexWriter against a Codec that resolves to these formats and the failure will only surface when fieldsWriter is invoked during the first flush — potentially after substantial work. The correct discipline is to detect 'read-only format selected as writer' at the earliest possible point (codec construction, or IndexWriter init) rather than at the first segment flush. Stating the precondition 'no writeable codec uses this format' would let it be checked once.

issues.description: Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat default constructor is 'protected' on a non-abstract class with no documented subclassing contract
issues.detail: The new test-only Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat declares a 'protected' sole constructor on a public, non-abstract class. There is no abstract method, no documented extension point, and no other subclass in the diff. This is a small thing, but the access modifier should reflect the actual invariant the class wants to defend. Either make the class abstract (and document what subclasses must do), or make the constructor package-private/public to match its actual use. Sloppy modifiers are how unstated preconditions accumulate.

issues.description: rawVectorFormat field visibility widened from private to package-private to allow access from the test-tree writer subclass
issues.detail: The change widens 'private static final FlatVectorsFormat rawVectorFormat' to package-private specifically so Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat (in the test tree) can read it. This is a coupling between production and test code that is invisible from the production class. Either pass the raw format in via a protected accessor with a documented contract, or accept that this class is now part of the testable surface and document it. The widening reads as incidental but is load-bearing for the test fixtures; that asymmetry should be stated.

review.summary: This patch moves a legacy scalar-quantized vector format into backward_codecs and forces it to be read-only by having fieldsWriter throw UnsupportedOperationException. The mechanical move is mostly clean, but the reasoning is incomplete in two structural ways. First, the read-only constraint is enforced by a runtime exception in a method whose type signature still promises a writer — a smuggled goto out of an advertised contract, which Dijkstra would refuse on principle: if the format cannot write, the type system should say so (split the interface, or fail at codec construction), not the body of a method that is reached only after a flush attempt. Second, DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT was previously a single named constant in the core flat-vector format and is now silently duplicated as a private 16 in the backward_codecs package — the invariant 'reader shift equals writer shift' is no longer expressible, and a future change to the core constant would corrupt reads of old indexes with no compile-time warning. Smaller issues compound the picture: @Deprecated was stripped from both classes at exactly the lifecycle moment it carries the most information for users; constructor parameters that gate merge concurrency are still validated but silently discarded; subclass-facing field visibility was downgraded from protected to package-private on a still-public abstract class without a stated rationale. The work is REASONED enough to move; it is TESTED-NOT-PROVED on the read-only invariant. The unstated preconditions ('this format is never used for writes', 'the disk shift never diverges from the core constant') need to be stated and mechanically enforced before merge.
